Rock.et: From Middle High German roc, from Old High German roc, from Proto-West Germanic *hrokk, from Proto-Germanic *hrukkaz, from Proto-Indo-European *rukn-, *ruk-, *rug-, *ruǵ- (“to spin”); or perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *kreḱ- (“to weave”). Doublet of Frack.
Borrowed from English rock, an ellipsis of rock and roll.

s: biker (a member of a motorcycle gang)
Rocker.et: From rocken + -er or Rock + -er. The "biker" sense is a pseudo-anglicism.

Rocken.et: From Middle High German rocke, from Old High German rocko, from Proto-West Germanic *rokkō, from Proto-Germanic *rukkô.

Roch.et: From Middle High German roch, from Arabic رُخّ (ruḵḵ), from Middle Persian lhw'. The /x/ must be compared to the word Schach. In both of these cases it is either due to direct borrowing from Arabic (during the Crusades) or alternatively to borrowing via Middle…

Roche.et: From Middle High German roc, from Old French roche, ultimately from Persian رخ (rox, “rook”).

Rockband.et: From Rock (“rock music”) + Band (“band”), borrowed from English rock band.
